ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Dome-shaped, red papules and nodules on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes in the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
key_facts: 12-year history of itchy eruptions over the whole body
Nodules appeared on the upper back 1 year previously and gradually increased in number and size
Patient denied a family history of inherited ichthyosis or atopy
Physical examination revealed extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Several 0.5- to 1-cm, dome-shaped, red papules and nodules were found on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes were observed on the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
Routine blood tests, biochemistry analyses, and peripheral blood flow cytometry tests were within normal limits
DNA analysis from paraffin sections showed clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor
Biopsy from back nodules showed atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis and extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis

shortlist: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive skin condition with itchy eruptions, nodules, and lymphadenopathy, consistent with clinical presentation and histopathology

shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to mycosis fungoides, with potential for systemic involvement

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category that encompasses mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome, with similar clinical and histopathological features

shortlist.label: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: CD4 positivity and small to medium-sized atypical lymphocytes on histopathology, consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Variant of mycosis fungoides with follicular involvement, consistent with clinical presentation and histopathology

raw.rationale: The patient's 12-year history of itchy eruptions, presence of dome-shaped nodules on the upper back, and extensive dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs, along with the histopathological findings of atrophy of the epidermis, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes, and epidermotropism, are characteristic of mycosis fungoides. The clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: Sézary syndrome typically presents with more widespread erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and atypical cells in the peripheral blood, which are not prominent in this case.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes mycosis fungoides, but the specific findings in this case are more consistent with mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium-sized pleomorphic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely due to the presence of epidermotropism and the long history of skin symptoms, which are more characteristic of mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: While this variant of mycosis fungoides can present with nodules, the lack of specific mention of follicular involvement in the histopathology makes this diagnosis less likely.
